segments: orders without recorded user_reasons or artifact_reasons
findings.hypothesis: A large portion of the top gap (lost: 417569) is unexplained by the recorded reason clusters (user_total: 199417 + artifact_total: 42107). The unexplained remainder appears concentrated in orders that did not surface a close-loop reason in the current artifacts/reason buckets; likely contributors include inventory/stock signals, item-count or price friction, or other upstream UX/validation delays.
findings.confirm_via: Drill a rate-bearing dimension that plausibly maps to missing signals (stock_status or item_count). If stock_status shows much lower confirmation rates for out-of-stock/backordered items, that would partition this unexplained loss. Alternatively run an experiment that surfaces inventory status earlier and measure confirmed rate lift.

findings.hypothesis: Orders flagged rx_gated have materially lower confirmation (rate: 0.3002) than non_rx (rate: 0.3904). That ~9 percentage-point gap means rx_gated contributes disproportionately to the top gap and could explain a non-trivial share of the 417569 lost orders.
findings.confirm_via: Run a targeted experiment to reduce rx-gated friction (e.g., pre-validate Rx or asynchronous clinic confirmation) and measure confirmed-rate change for rx_gated; or drill further (stock_status / item_count) within rx_gated vs non_rx to see if other covariates explain the gap.

next_question.rationale: stock_status is a rate-bearing dimension not yet tried (listed in rate_bearing_not_yet_tried) and plausibly maps to the unexplained loss: 'items unavailable' appears in user_reasons (3907) and artifact-level issues exist (artifact_total: 42107). Drilling stock_status can partition confirmation rates for in-stock vs backordered/out-of-stock items and either attribute unexplained losses to inventory problems or rule that out before spending budget on other cuts.
